summary: Adobe's launch page for an open-source Pan-CJK serif (2017), laid out like a long press article in black-and-white line art: a hero grid mixing Chinese, Japanese and Korean characters on writing-practice cells, a video, big glyph statistics, line-drawn mock software UIs, a four-region comparison of one code point with a 'Spot the differences' button, a weight row with a one-character tester, line-portrait team bios and a grid of Typekit cards plus download links. A corporate, multi-partner (Adobe, Google, Sandoll, Iwata, SinoType) voice; the whole page, UI included, is set in the typeface and localised in five languages.

instances.look: Static top strip: Adobe logo at the left, a language switcher 'English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어' (current greyed) at the right, all set in Source Han Serif
Fixed at the right edge (stitched over many crops): three small outlined boxes stacked vertically, 'STORY', 'TEAM', 'FONTS', jumping to #story, #team and #get-the-fonts

instances.variantDefinition: The first screen is a small name and subtitle over a large uniform grid of characters drawn from every script or language the family covers (often on writing-practice guide lines and bleeding off the page); the coverage itself is the first impression.
instances.look: White page: 'Source Han Serif' in bold serif and 'An open source Pan-CJK typeface' below it, then a 5-row grid of characters mixing Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, Japanese kana and Korean hangul (社 시 此 십 べ キ 포 現 …), each in a square cell with faint diagonal and centre guide lines like a calligraphy practice sheet; the grid bleeds off the left edge
instances.ux: A short loader first (a boxed '源' turning like a cube, ~1s); then static; section jumps via the fixed STORY / TEAM / FONTS tabs
instances.learn: Interleave the scripts cell by cell instead of grouping them: one grid says 'four languages, one design' before any text, and the 米字格 guide lines frame them in a shared tradition
